I’ll trace how server-info requests are routed, add dedicated capacity, and check that the response and authentication behavior stay compatible. I’m using the repository’s Python style skill for the change and tests.

The shared worker limit is in the ASGI-to-Flask adapter. I’ll give server-info requests a separate limit there, so they retain the existing Flask handler, response, and authentication rules. Gunicorn and Waitress will continue using the unchanged Flask path.

The new regression cases passed for both API paths, with and without a static prefix, while all shared worker capacity was occupied. They also verified anonymous access and byte-for-byte equality with the Flask response. I found that the auth bypass needed an exact server-info route entry and added it. Pytest’s final report hit a sandbox restriction on process inspection after the tests passed.

Implemented dedicated worker capacity for both server-info paths, including custom static prefixes. Requests now bypass the exhausted shared limit while retaining the existing Flask response and Gunicorn/Waitress compatibility. Added exact authentication exemptions for anonymous discovery.

Regression coverage checks saturation, response equality, prefixes, and authentication boundaries. All 22 executed tests passed; two runs encountered a sandbox process-inspection error during final reporting. No dependencies installed or full suite run.
